stories.head: WorldParticle unifies particle-based physical simulation
stories.fact: MIT and collaborators describe WorldParticle, a deep-learning architecture that represents materials as particles and predicts their next movements across physical phenomena, including granular materials and proteins.
stories.why: For MATLAB surrogate models, test shared representations against specialist baselines and measure long-rollout stability.
stories.unc: Research demonstrations do not establish universal physical fidelity or applicability to financial prices.
stories.alt: Conceptual labels connect materials to particle representations and next-step dynamics, with separate regime and rollout checks.

stories.head: New review separates agentic finance capability from prediction
stories.fact: A scoping review synthesizes 165 studies from 2023–2026. Its framework distinguishes prediction, interpretation, recommendation, execution and coordination, and explicitly separates historical or simulated evaluation from live or forward testing.
stories.why: Require evidence for the decision responsibility an agent actually assumes; preserve external risk controls and forward evaluation.
stories.unc: A literature synthesis is not a validated profitable strategy. Tool use alone does not establish agentic capability.
stories.alt: Four labels identify the review corpus, distinguish prediction from execution, distinguish backtests from live evidence, and require governance evidence.

stories.head: Index futures rebound, with Nasdaq trailing the Dow
stories.fact: At 6:39 a.m. EST, Reuters reported Dow futures up 1.06%, S&P 500 futures up 0.66%, and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.42% following last week’s selloff.
stories.why: Check breadth and ES/NQ relative strength before treating the rebound as broad risk recovery.
stories.unc: Reported snapshot, not executable quotes. Positive futures do not establish healthy order-book depth.
stories.alt: Labels compare three reported futures percentage changes at the same November 9 checkpoint.

stories.head: Fed reports faster September consumer-credit growth
stories.fact: Consumer credit grew at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 6.4% in September and 4.2% in Q3. September revolving credit grew 14.5% annualized, versus 3.6% for nonrevolving credit.
stories.why: Separate revolving from nonrevolving borrowing when testing consumer-demand and credit-risk signals.
stories.unc: Preliminary and revisable; annualized growth is not a monthly percentage change, and borrowing growth alone does not prove household distress.
stories.alt: Separate labels show September annualized total, revolving and nonrevolving credit growth, marked seasonally adjusted and preliminary.

stories.head: KKR reports record adjusted earnings and fee growth
stories.fact: KKR reports Q3 adjusted net income of $1.6 billion, up 29% year over year, and fee-related earnings of $1.3 billion, up 27%. Assets under management reached $804 billion.
stories.why: Separate recurring fee earnings from realization-sensitive income when assessing alternative asset managers.
stories.unc: Adjusted measures are non-GAAP; AUM is not revenue or immediately deployable liquidity.
stories.credit: KKR Q3 release, November 9, 2026; SEC exhibit
stories.alt: Labels separately show adjusted income, fee-related earnings and assets under management; measures are not added together.
